questions.prompt: Which part of a flowering plant usually absorbs water from soil?
questions.explanation: Roots take in water and dissolved minerals from the soil.

questions.prompt: What causes a shadow to form?
questions.explanation: A shadow appears where an opaque object prevents light from reaching a surface.

questions.prompt: When liquid water becomes water vapour, the change is called what?
questions.explanation: Evaporation is the change from liquid water to water vapour.

questions.prompt: What mainly causes day and night on Earth?
questions.explanation: As Earth rotates, different parts face towards and then away from the Sun.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Connect rotation with day and night

questions.prompt: Which material is most likely to conduct electricity well?
questions.explanation: Copper is a metal and a good electrical conductor.

questions.prompt: Which animal is a vertebrate?
questions.explanation: A lizard has a backbone; the other animals do not.

questions.prompt: Sugar seems to disappear when stirred into warm water. What has happened?
questions.explanation: The sugar particles spread through the water to form a solution.

questions.prompt: In a fair test, how many factors should be deliberately changed?
questions.explanation: Changing one factor allows its effect to be compared fairly.

questions.prompt: What produces the sound from a plucked guitar string?
questions.explanation: The vibrating string makes nearby air vibrate, producing sound.

questions.prompt: Which property is typical of a solid?
questions.explanation: A solid normally keeps a fixed shape and volume.

questions.prompt: Why can the Moon be seen from Earth even though it does not make its own visible light?
questions.explanation: Sunlight reflects from the Moon's surface towards Earth.

questions.prompt: What role do fungi often have in a forest ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Many fungi break down dead matter and return nutrients to the soil.

questions.prompt: Which tool is designed to measure temperature?
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures how hot or cold something is.

questions.prompt: Two identical ice cubes are placed on a metal tray and a wooden board in the same room. The cube on metal melts first. What is the best explanation?

options.text: Metal is always hotter than wood

questions.explanation: Metal conducts thermal energy to the ice more quickly than wood.

questions.prompt: A seedling bends towards a window. Which response is being shown?
questions.explanation: The shoot grows towards the strongest light source.

questions.prompt: A puddle dries faster on a windy day. Why?

options.text: Wind adds salt to the water
Moving air carries water vapour away

questions.explanation: Removing moist air above the puddle allows evaporation to continue faster.

questions.prompt: A torch circuit has a fresh cell and working globe but a gap between two wires. Why is the globe off?

options.text: The cell has too much energy

questions.explanation: Current needs a complete conducting path; the gap makes the circuit open.

questions.prompt: A student tests how ramp height affects toy-car travel distance. What should be measured?
questions.explanation: Travel distance is the dependent variable named in the investigation question.

questions.prompt: A fossil shell is found in rock far inland. What is the strongest inference?

options.text: The rock formed inside a tree
The area was once under water

questions.explanation: A marine fossil indicates that the environment was under water when the sediment formed.

questions.prompt: Four powders look alike. Which test gives the strongest evidence that they are different substances?

options.text: Give each powder a different name
Place each powder in a different-shaped dish
Look at each powder from farther away
Compare several properties such as solubility and reaction with vinegar

questions.explanation: A pattern across several observable tests provides evidence beyond appearance alone.

questions.prompt: A food chain's arrows show the direction in which energy is transferred.
questions.explanation: Energy moves from the organism being eaten to the organism that eats it.

questions.prompt: The pitch of a sound tells how loud the sound is.
questions.explanation: Pitch describes how high or low a sound is; volume describes loudness.

questions.prompt: Condensation can form when water vapour cools.
questions.explanation: Cooling water vapour can turn it into liquid droplets.

questions.prompt: A magnet attracts every metal.
questions.explanation: Magnets attract some metals, such as iron and steel, but not all metals.

questions.prompt: A controlled variable is kept the same during a fair test.
questions.explanation: Keeping other factors constant makes the effect of the changed variable clearer.

questions.prompt: All changes that make a new substance are easily reversed.
questions.explanation: Many changes that form new substances are difficult or impossible to reverse.

questions.prompt: Earth takes about one year to complete one orbit of the Sun.
questions.explanation: One revolution around the Sun defines a year.

questions.prompt: A larger sample always removes every source of error from an investigation.
questions.explanation: A larger sample can improve reliability, but poor measurement or unfair testing can still cause error.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Evaluate a claim about sample size

questions.prompt: Which TWO features help many desert plants conserve water?
questions.explanation: A waxy surface slows water loss and reduced leaves expose less surface area.

questions.prompt: Which TWO actions would increase the rate at which a wet cloth dries?

options.text: Place it in still, humid air
Fold it into a tight bundle

questions.explanation: Spreading increases exposed area and moving air removes water vapour.

questions.prompt: Which TWO are evidence that a chemical change may have occurred?
questions.explanation: Gas production and an unexpected colour change can indicate new substances.

questions.prompt: Which TWO observations are measurements rather than opinions?
questions.explanation: Height and temperature use stated units and can be checked objectively.

questions.prompt: Which TWO changes would make an electromagnet stronger?

options.text: Replace the iron core with paper

questions.explanation: More coils and greater current produce a stronger magnetic field.

questions.prompt: Which TWO statements correctly compare weather and climate?
questions.explanation: Weather is current or short-term; climate summarises patterns over many years.

questions.prompt: Which TWO features should be the same when comparing fertilisers on seedlings?
questions.explanation: Seedling type and pot size should be controlled while fertiliser is changed.

questions.prompt: Which TWO conclusions are supported if three repeated trials give 18 cm, 19 cm and 18 cm?

options.text: The exact true value must be 18 cm

questions.explanation: The close results are consistent, and repetition gives more confidence without proving an exact value.

questions.prompt: Order these stages in a simple flowering-plant life cycle.
questions.explanation: A seed germinates, grows into a seedling and then an adult flowering plant, which produces seeds that disperse.

questions.prompt: Order the energy transfers when a battery-powered lamp shines.
questions.explanation: Stored chemical energy becomes electrical energy, then the globe changes it to light and heat before light spreads.

items.text: Chemical energy is stored in the cell
Electrical energy moves through the circuit
The globe changes electrical energy to light and heat

questions.prompt: Order the steps for investigating whether salt changes water's freezing time.
questions.explanation: Use equal volumes, vary measured salt amounts, record times, then repeat and compare averages.

questions.prompt: Order these events in sedimentary rock formation.
questions.explanation: Weathering makes particles, transport deposits them, layers accumulate, and pressure plus cementation forms rock.
